text.title: User Research at Scale Examples
text.summary: End-to-end worked example illustrating the methodology against a realistic input.

example.title: Weekly onboarding-friction study (N=612)
example.note: Intake queue: 612 sessions across 3 segments (free, paid, churned). Sampling: stratified by segment + tenure; recruit hit target. Transcribed via Otter (interviewer turns stripped via Looppanel). Frozen codebook of 84 codes applied via Sonnet batch; 14 novel themes parked in proposed_codes. Synthesizer (Opus) emitted 5 candidate findings; HITL review accepted 3 (>=50 evidence each), rejected 2 (<50 evidence). Accepted code: 'template_anxiety'; merged into book v37. Report published; throughput dashboard updated; no PII left ZDR endpoints.

example.title: Theme-coder prompt
example.note: Theme-coder prompt with frozen codebook and proposed_codes channel:
example.code: <task>code-transcript</task> <codebook src=".aidocs/research/codebook.yaml"/> <rules> <rule>One quote may receive multiple codes; record span offsets.</rule> <rule>Reject codes not in codebook. Emit proposed_codes list instead.</rule> <rule>Tag valence in {-2,-1,0,1,2} with one-line evidence.</rule> <rule>If transcript is less than 80% English confidence, halt and request translation.</rule> </rules> <output schema="coded_quote_v1">JSONL</output> <gotcha>Do not summarize. Preserve verbatim spans.</gotcha>
example.note: Enforces rule frozen-codebook-plus-overflow; the span-offset rule is what the hallucinated-participant-ids antipattern relies on.
